issues.description: The problem statement and the template code describe and use a parameterless messageOnRide() method (signature: messageOnRide(): String), but the solution implementation defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and corresponding implementations in Pig and Seal. This parameter mismatch is structural: students following the problem/spec/template will implement or call messageOnRide() without parameters, but the provided solution uses a different signature, causing confusion and compilation/signature incompatibility between expected and provided code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to implement messageOnRide() with no parameters (String messageOnRide()) and update Pig/Seal implementations accordingly, or (B) update the problem statement and template examples to require messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust the sample calls (e.g., r.messageOnRide(5)). Ensure all references, UML, and example code use the same signature.

issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method is specified in the problem statement and used in the template as a no-argument method returning a String, but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) (and Pig/Seal implement the version with an int parameter). This changes the public API and return formatting expectations and will confuse students who follow the problem/template (which expect messageOnRide()) versus the solution (which requires an int).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable API consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by declaring String messageOnRide() in Rideable and update Pig and Seal to implement messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify messageOnRide(int speed) and the exact return format including the speed. Prefer (A) to align with the current exercise description and template usage.
